review.notes: Built on the course: six-part email, BLUF, register, false friends, grammar traps, send checklist, meeting stages, agreeing, polite disagreement, clarifying, video calls, actions, politeness ladder, conditionals, softening, negotiation stages. Fictional companies.

content.company: Bridgeport Logistics (fictional), working with an English-speaking supplier and client
content.briefing: This week you work in English: emails to a new supplier, a video meeting with a client, and a short negotiation. Your English must be clear, polite and correct, so nothing is misunderstood.

variants.text: You need the supplier to confirm a delivery date by Thursday. How does your email start after the greeting?

choices.t: 'Could you confirm the delivery date by Thursday?'
choices.f: BLUF: the purpose in the first sentence.

choices.t: 'As you know, our company was founded in 2009...'
'I am writing to you about several things.'
choices.f: Vague; the reader still does not know what you need.

variants.text: Which subject line is best?

choices.f: Topic and action in the subject line.

variants.text: You write a complaint to a new client about damaged goods. Which register?

choices.f: Formal for new contacts, complaints and legal matters.
Too casual for a complaint to a new contact.

variants.text: How do you end an email with a clear call to action?

choices.t: 'Please send the revised price by Friday.'
'Let me know what you think about it all.'
choices.f: Polite, but no clear action or date.

choices.t: 'Bye for now, talk soon, all the best.'

variants.text: You want to say 'I intend to visit you in May'. Which sentence is correct?

choices.t: 'I intend to visit you in May.'
'I pretend to visit you in May.'
choices.f: False friend: it means you will fake a visit.

choices.t: 'I attend to visit you in May.'

variants.text: You mean 'at the moment, we have no stock'. Which is correct?
Which sentence is correct?
Which sentence is correct?
The client proposes daily deliveries. Your warehouse is at 90% capacity. How do you disagree politely?

choices.t: 'I see your point, but we're at 90%. Could we try three days a week?'
'No, that is completely impossible for us, so please forget the idea.'
choices.f: Too direct for a client; no reason or option.

choices.t: 'OK, maybe, we will see what happens with deliveries later on, perhaps.'
choices.f: Unclear; the client thinks you agreed.

variants.text: You partly agree with a colleague's idea. What do you say?
On a video call you missed a key number. What do you say?

choices.t: 'Sorry, could you repeat the last figure?'
Nod and hope it is in the minutes

choices.f: Too abrupt for a client meeting.

variants.text: A participant is speaking but nobody can hear him. What do you say?

choices.f: Volume is not the problem; mute is.

variants.text: At the end of the meeting, how do you confirm an action?

choices.t: 'Ana will send the revised plan by Friday.'
choices.f: Who, what, when. Then send it in writing.

variants.text: In which order does a well-run meeting go?

choices.t: Discuss first, set the purpose at the end

variants.text: Which request is the most polite?

choices.t: 'Would you mind sending the price list?'

choices.f: Polite, but less formal than 'would you mind'.

variants.text: You offer a deal: payment terms in return for a fast decision. Which sentence?

choices.t: 'If you confirm today, we will pay 30% in advance.'
choices.f: First conditional for a real offer.

choices.t: 'If you confirm today, we would paid 30% in advance.'
choices.f: Grammar error: 'would pay', and it weakens the offer.

choices.t: 'If you will confirm today, we pay 30%.'
choices.f: Not 'if you will'; and the result needs 'will'.

variants.text: You must say the price is too high, but keep the relationship. Which is best?

choices.t: 'I'm afraid the price seems a little high for us.'
choices.f: Softening language keeps it polite and clear.

choices.t: 'Your price is too expensive and bad.'
'The price is OK, I think, maybe.'
choices.f: So soft the message is lost.

variants.text: The negotiation is agreed verbally. What is the last stage?

choices.t: Nothing; a verbal deal is enough

variants.text: Before you press send, what do you check?

choices.f: The send checklist catches most problems.

choices.t: Only the spelling of the person's name
Nothing; it is better to send quickly

variants.text: Which closing fits a neutral business email?
